questions.question: The rate of nickel plating on a metal is ₹50 / m². If the cost of nickel plating on a curved surface area of a solid hemisphere is ₹600, find the cost of nickel coating on the total surface area of this hemisphere.
questions.solution:

Cost of nickel plating per m² = ₹50

Cost of nickel plating on curved surface area (CSA) = ₹600

**Formula used:**

CSA of a hemisphere = 2πr²

Total surface area (TSA) of a hemisphere = 3πr²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of CSA = (600)/(50)

⇒ Area of CSA = 12 m²

CSA of hemisphere = 2πr²

⇒ 2πr² = 12

⇒ r² = (12)/(2π)

⇒ r² = (6)/(π)

Total surface area (TSA) = 3πr²

⇒ TSA = 3π × (6)/(π)

⇒ TSA = 18 m²

Cost of TSA = TSA × cost per m²

⇒ Cost of TSA = 18 × 50

⇒ Cost of TSA = ₹900

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: A shopkeeper claims that he sells rock salt at ₹23 per kg, which costs him ₹25 per kg. But he gives 800 g instead of 1,000 g. What is his percentage profit or loss?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Claimed selling price (S.P.꜀ₗₐᵢₘₑd) = ₹23 per kg

Cost price (C.P.) = ₹25 per kg

Weight given = 800 g instead of 1000 g

**Formula used:**

Actual C.P. for quantity sold = C.P. per kg × Actual quantity sold

Actual S.P. for quantity sold = S.P. per kg (claimed) × Actual quantity delivered

Percentage Profit/Loss = dfrac{{(Actual S.P. - Actual C.P.)}}{{Actual C.P.}} times 100

**Calculations:**

Let's consider the cost and selling price for the quantity of goods involved in the transaction.

The shopkeeper sells 800 g of salt, but charges for 1000 g.

C.P. of 1000 g (1 kg) = ₹25

C.P. of 1 g = dfrac{25}{1000}

C.P. of 800 g = dfrac{25}{1000} times 800

⇒ Actual C.P. = dfrac{25 times 8}{10} = dfrac{200}{10} = ₹20

So, the shopkeeper spent ₹20 to acquire the 800 g of salt he actually gives to the customer.

The shopkeeper claims to sell at ₹23 per kg (which means per 1000 g).

The customer pays for 1000 g at the claimed selling price.

S.P. received = ₹23

Actual S.P. (amount received from customer for what they believe is 1kg) = ₹23

Actual C.P. (cost to shopkeeper for the 800g actually given) = ₹20

Since Actual S.P. > Actual C.P., there is a profit.

Profit = Actual S.P. - Actual C.P. = ₹23 - ₹20 = ₹3

Percentage Profit = dfrac{{Profit}}{{Actual C.P.}} times 100

⇒ Percentage Profit = dfrac{3}{20} times 100

⇒ Percentage Profit = 3 × 5

⇒ Percentage Profit = 15%

**∴ The shopkeeper makes a profit of 15%.**

Remaining time = 1 - 1/3 = 2/3 hour

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

⇒ Speed = 6 × (3/2)

⇒ Speed = 9 km/h

questions.question: The LCM of x³ - 27, x² - x - 6, x+2 is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The expressions are: x³ - 27, x² - x - 6, and x+2

**Formula used:**

Algebraic factorization formulas:

a³ - b³ = (a - b)(a² + ab + b²)

For quadratic expressions of the form ax² + bx + c, factorize by splitting the middle term.

L.C.M. is the product of the highest powers of all prime factors (distinct factors) present in the expressions.

Calculations:

Expression 1: x³ - 27

This is in the form a³ - b³, where a = x and b = 3.

⇒ x³ - 27 = (x - 3)(x² + 3x + 3²)

⇒ x³ - 27 = (x - 3)(x² + 3x + 9)

Expression 2: x² - x - 6

Factorize the quadratic by splitting the middle term (-x) into terms whose product is 1 × (-6) = -6 and whose sum is -1. These terms are -3x and +2x.

⇒ x² - 3x + 2x - 6

⇒ x(x - 3) + 2(x - 3)

⇒ (x - 3)(x + 2)

Expression 3: x+2

This expression is already in its simplest factored form.

The L.C.M. of the factored expressions.

The factored expressions are:

(x - 3)(x² + 3x + 9)

(x - 3)(x + 2)

(x + 2)

Identify all distinct factors and their highest powers:

Factor (x - 3): Highest power is 1.

Factor (x² + 3x + 9): Highest power is 1.

Factor (x + 2): Highest power is 1.

L.C.M. = Product of these distinct factors with their highest powers

⇒ L.C.M. = (x - 3) times (x² + 3x + 9) times (x + 2)

**∴ The L.C.M. of the given expressions is (x - 3)(x + 2)(x² + 3x + 9).**

One diagonal = 30 cm

**Formula used:**

Where d₁ and d₂ are the diagonals of the rhombus.

**Calculation:**

Side of rhombus = 68 ÷ 4

⇒ Side = 17 cm

Using Pythagoras theorem:

(Diagonal₂/2)² + (Diagonal₁/2)² = Side²

⇒ (d₂/2)² + (30/2)² = 17²

⇒ (d₂/2)² + 15² = 289

⇒ (d₂/2)² + 225 = 289

⇒ (d₂/2)² = 289 - 225

⇒ (d₂/2)² = 64

⇒ d₂/2 = √64

⇒ d₂/2 = 8

⇒ d₂ = 8 × 2

⇒ d₂ = 16 cm

Area of rhombus = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂

⇒ Area = (1/2) × 30 × 16

⇒ Area = 240 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: Riya sold two packets of detergent at ₹96 each. On one packet she gains 20% and on the other, she loses 20%. The net gain or loss in the complete process is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling Price of first packet (S.P.₁) = ₹96

Selling Price of second packet (S.P.₂) = ₹96

Gain on first packet = 20%

Loss on second packet = 20%

**Formula used:**

If S.P. and gain/loss percentage are known, C.P. can be found using:

C.P. = dfrac{{S.P.}}{(1 + frac{{Gain%}}{100})} for gain

C.P. = dfrac{{S.P.}}{(1 - frac{{Loss%}}{100})} for loss

Total C.P. = C.P.₁ + C.P.₂

Total S.P. = S.P.₁ + S.P.₂

Percentage Loss = dfrac{{Total Loss}}{{Total C.P.}} times 100

**Calculations:**

**For the first packet (20% gain):**

C.P.₁ = dfrac{96}{(1 + (20)/(100))} = dfrac{96}{(1 + (1)/(5))} = dfrac{96}{(6)/(5)}

⇒ C.P.₁ = dfrac{96 times 5}{6} = 16 × 5 = ₹80

**For the second packet (20% loss):**

C.P.₂ = dfrac{96}{(1 - (20)/(100))} = dfrac{96}{(1 - (1)/(5))} = dfrac{96}{(4)/(5)}

⇒ C.P.₂ = dfrac{96 times 5}{4} = 24 × 5 = ₹120

Total C.P. = C.P.₁ + C.P.₂ = ₹80 + ₹120 = ₹200

Total S.P. = S.P.₁ + S.P.₂ = ₹96 + ₹96 = ₹192

Since Total S.P. < Total C.P., there is a loss.

Total Loss = Total C.P. - Total S.P. = ₹200 - ₹192 = ₹8

**∴ The net loss in the complete process is ₹8.**

questions.question:
A shopkeeper offered following four different discount schemes for buyers on an item.

A. Two successive discounts of 8%.

B. A discount of 11% followed by a discount of 5%.

C. Successive discounts of 13% and 3%

D. A discount of 16%.

Which discount scheme should be opted for getting the item at minimum price?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For successive discounts x% and y%, the effective single discount is [x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100]%.

When the sum of discounts (x + y) is equal, the effective discount is maximum when the product (x × y) is minimum.

The sum in all schemes is 16%. The products are: A → 64, B → 55, C → 39, D → 0.

Scheme D has the minimum product (0), thus giving the maximum effective discount of 16%.

The maximum discount directly results in the minimum selling price for the buyer.

**∴ The correct answer is Scheme D.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Four discount schemes for an item:

A. Two successive discounts of 8%.

B. A discount of 11% followed by a discount of 5%.

C. Successive discounts of 13% and 3%.

D. A single discount of 16%.

**Formula Used:**

Effective discount for successive discounts x% and y% = [x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100]%

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/015494cf1f78b4bd1068f752d73a50454d9d33937d16aa8afa467e111bcf55ec.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the Marked Price (MP) of the item be 100.

⇒ For Scheme A: Effective Discount = 8 + 8 − (8 × 8) ÷ 100 = 16 − 0.64 = 15.36%

⇒ SP for Scheme A = 100 − 15.36 = 84.64

⇒ For Scheme B: Effective Discount = 11 + 5 − (11 × 5) ÷ 100 = 16 − 0.55 = 15.45%

⇒ SP for Scheme B = 100 − 15.45 = 84.55

⇒ For Scheme C: Effective Discount = 13 + 3 − (13 × 3) ÷ 100 = 16 − 0.39 = 15.61%

⇒ SP for Scheme C = 100 − 15.61 = 84.39

⇒ For Scheme D: Single discount is 16%

⇒ SP for Scheme D = 100 − 16 = 84.00

⇒ Comparing all selling prices, Scheme D provides the item at the minimum selling price (84.00).

**∴ The correct answer is Scheme D.**

**__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

When two discounts of a% and b% are given successively, the equivalent single discount is given by: [a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100]%.

Maximizing Discount Trick

If the sum of two successive discounts is constant, the effective discount is maximized when the difference between the two discount values is maximum (i.e., their product is minimum).

Marked Price vs Selling Price

Marked Price (MP) is the original price tag of the item. Selling Price (SP) is the price after applying the discount. SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

questions.question: What is the term for the maximum population size that an environment can sustain indefinitely?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carrying capacity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Carrying capacity** refers to the maximum population size of a species that an environment can sustain indefinitely without degrading the ecosystem.
 
• It is determined by the availability of resources such as food, water, shelter, and other ecological factors.
 
• When a population exceeds its carrying capacity, resources become depleted, leading to competition, starvation, or population decline.
 
• Carrying capacity is dynamic and can fluctuate due to changes in environmental conditions, resource availability, or human intervention.
 
• It is a central concept in ecology and environmental science, helping to understand the sustainability of ecosystems and species populations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ecological Niche**: Refers to the role and position a species has in its environment, including its interactions with other species and its use of resources.
 
• **Pioneer Species**: These are the first species to colonize barren or disturbed environments, initiating ecological succession and creating conditions for other species to thrive.
 
• **Biotic Potential**: It is the maximum reproductive capacity of an organism under optimal environmental conditions, without limiting factors like food shortage or predation.
 
• **Limiting Factors**: Environmental factors such as nutrient availability, climate, and predation that restrict the growth of a population and help determine its carrying capacity.
 
• **Human Impact**: Activities like deforestation, urbanization, and pollution can reduce the carrying capacity of ecosystems by depleting resources or altering environmental conditions.

questions.question: In the Vedic period, education was begun with which of the following?

• **Upanayana** was a sacred thread ceremony in the Vedic period that marked the formal beginning of education for boys, particularly in the Brahmin, Kshatriya, and Vaishya varnas.
 
• This ceremony symbolized the initiation of students into **Brahmacharya** (the student phase of life), where they would live and study with a Guru.
 
• The child was taught to recite the **Gayatri Mantra** during this ceremony, which was considered a key step in spiritual and educational growth.
 
• The education received post-Upanayana focused on the **Vedas, rituals, philosophy, and other branches of knowledge**, emphasizing both spiritual and practical learning.
 
• Only boys of the upper three varnas (Brahmins, Kshatriyas, and Vaishyas) were eligible for the Upanayana ceremony during the Vedic period.

• **Vanaprastha:** The third stage of life, where individuals transition from household duties to a more spiritual lifestyle, often retreating to the forest for contemplation and penance.
 
• **Niyoga:** A Vedic practice allowing a childless widow or a husband with no offspring to have children through a designated person, primarily for lineage continuation. This practice was unrelated to education.
 
• **Brahmacharya:** The first stage of life in the Vedic system, focusing on learning, discipline, and self-control. The Upanayana ceremony marked the start of this phase.
 
• **Gayatri Mantra:** A highly revered hymn from the Rigveda chanted during the Upanayana ceremony. It is considered a key spiritual and meditative tool in Vedic education.

__
 
• The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first significant intervention by the British government in the East India Company's affairs, marking the beginning of parliamentary control over the Company.
 
• The Act was introduced to address administrative and financial issues arising from the Company's territorial expansion in India, particularly after the Battle of Buxar (1764).
 
• It established a Governor-General of Bengal (along with a council of four members) to centralize administration, with Warren Hastings as the first Governor-General.
 
• The Act also created the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William (Calcutta) in 1774 to improve the legal framework in British-controlled territories.
 
• It laid the foundation for future legislative and administrative reforms, eventually leading to the Government of India Act, 1858, which abolished Company rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Governor-General of Bengal:** The Regulating Act empowered the Governor-General and his council to oversee the administration of Bengal, Madras, and Bombay, making it a central authority.
 
• **Supreme Court of Judicature:** Established under the Act, it was the first British court in India with jurisdiction over British subjects and Company employees.
 
• **Charter Acts:** Later Acts, like the Charter Act of 1793 and Charter Act of 1813, further regulated the Company's activities, including trade and governance.
 
• **Pitt's India Act, 1784:** While significant, this Act came after the Regulating Act and focused on creating a dual system of governance between the Company and the British Crown.

• Anaemia can be caused by nutritional deficiencies (e.g., lack of iron, vitamin B12, or folate), chronic diseases, or genetic disorders like sickle cell anaemia.
 
• The most common type of anaemia worldwide is **iron-deficiency anaemia**, which occurs due to insufficient iron intake or absorption.
 
• Treatment typically involves addressing the underlying cause, such as dietary changes, supplements, or medical procedures.

• **Iron-Deficiency Anaemia:** The most common form of anaemia, often caused by poor dietary intake, blood loss, or issues with iron absorption.
 
• **Pernicious Anaemia:** A type of anaemia caused by the inability to absorb vitamin B12, often due to autoimmune conditions affecting the stomach lining.
 
• **Thalassemia:** A genetic disorder resulting in abnormal hemoglobin production, leading to chronic anaemia.

questions.question: The space-filling model emphasises the relative size of each atom based on its ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**van der Waals radius**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The space-filling model represents atoms as spheres with sizes proportional to their **van der Waals radii**.
 
• **Van der Waals radius** defines the effective size of an atom when it is not bonded to another atom, representing its physical boundary.
 
• In the space-filling model, overlapping spheres illustrate the physical arrangement of atoms in a molecule, showcasing their spatial proximity.
 
• This model is particularly useful for visualizing the overall shape, volume, and close-packing of molecules.
 
• It emphasizes the steric factors and spatial constraints, which are crucial in molecular interactions, such as protein-ligand binding or crystal packing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Covalent Radius**: The covalent radius refers to half the distance between the nuclei of two identical atoms bonded covalently. It is smaller than the van der Waals radius since atoms are closer in bonded states.
 
• **Ionic Radius**: This is the effective radius of an ion in a crystal lattice. It depends on the ion's charge and coordination number, differing significantly from the van der Waals radius.
 
• **Van der Waals Forces**: Weak intermolecular forces arising from temporary dipoles in atoms or molecules. The van der Waals radius is a measure of the distance where these forces become significant.
 
• **Space-Filling Model Applications**: These models are widely used in structural biology and materials science to study molecular shape, packing, and steric hindrance.
 
• **Limitations of the Space-Filling Model**: Although visually intuitive, it may obscure detailed bonding information and is less effective for depicting smaller molecules or bond-specific interactions.

• The Northern Plains are formed by the alluvial deposits of rivers originating from the Himalayas, making them ideal for the formation of such fertile regions.
 
• Doabs support extensive agriculture, including crops such as wheat, rice, and sugarcane, contributing significantly to India's food grain production.

questions.question: The Indian Constitution originally consisted of how many Articles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**395**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Constitution of India originally consisted of **395 Articles** divided into 22 Parts and 8 Schedules when it was adopted on 26 November 1949.
 
• The Indian Constitution is one of the **longest written constitutions** in the world.
 
• It came into effect on **26 January 1950**, celebrated annually as Republic Day in India.
 
• Over time, the Constitution has undergone several amendments, and as of 2023, there are **470 Articles** divided into 25 Parts and 12 Schedules.
 
• The framing of the Constitution was led by the **Constituent Assembly**, chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, who is also known as the "Father of the Indian Constitution."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parts of the Constitution:** Initially, the Constitution had 22 Parts which outlined the framework of governance, fundamental rights, directive principles, and other provisions.
 
• **Schedules:** The original 8 Schedules provided detailed information regarding languages, allocation of powers, and more. Now, the Constitution includes 12 Schedules.
 
• **Amendments:** The Constitution has been amended multiple times. The first amendment was enacted in 1951, and as of 2023, there are 105 amendments.
 
• **Drafting Process:** The drafting of the Constitution took around 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days. The final draft was adopted on 26 November 1949.
 
• **Significance:** The Indian Constitution is unique as it incorporates features from various global constitutions, such as the parliamentary system from the UK, the federal structure from the USA, and directive principles from Ireland.

questions.question: Water from melting snow or rainfall or the spring drains downwards through an area of land and finally gets mixed into a large water body like river or ocean. This area of land is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Drainage Basin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **drainage basin**, also known as a watershed, is a geographical area where all precipitation collects and drains into a common outlet, such as a river, lake, or ocean.
 
• It includes surface runoff, groundwater flow, and streams that contribute to the main water body.
 
• The boundaries of a drainage basin are defined by elevated terrain called **drainage divides** or ridgelines.
 
• Examples of major drainage basins include the Ganges-Brahmaputra Basin in South Asia and the Amazon Basin in South America.
 
• Drainage basins are critical for understanding water resource management, flood control, and ecosystem sustainability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bay:** A bay is a body of water partially enclosed by land but connected to a larger water body, such as an ocean or sea. Bays are not part of drainage basins as they do not collect and channel water.
 
• **Estuary:** An estuary is a coastal water body where freshwater from rivers meets and mixes with saltwater from the sea. It is a transitional zone and not synonymous with a drainage basin.
 
• **Delta:** A delta is a landform created at the mouth of a river, where it deposits sediment as it flows into a larger water body. While deltas are part of river systems, they are distinct from drainage basins.
 
• **Hydrological Cycle:** Drainage basins play a key role in the hydrological cycle by collecting precipitation and channeling it through streams and rivers into larger water bodies.
 
• **Human Impact:** Human activities such as deforestation, urbanization, and dam construction can alter the natural functioning of drainage basins, affecting water quality and flow patterns.
